claude.sample_unit: clinical scenario questions (plus 103 multiple-choice questions; 7 questions in prompt phase)

links.outcome: Output stability (score variance) across three repeated generations for each model
links.effect: GPT-4o had lowest variance; Deepseek-V2.5 highest and most unstable. GPT-4o variance significantly lower than others in accuracy, completeness, safety, practicality (corrected p<0.005).
links.quote: Among all five models, GPT-4o exhibited the lowest overall variance, indicating the most consistent output. Deepseek-V2.5 exhibited the highest variance, reflecting the most unstable performance.

links.outcome: Gap between exam-style MCQ accuracy and clinical scenario response quality/safety
links.effect: All models exceeded 90% MCQ accuracy, but clinical scenarios yielded low-scoring responses (Deepseek-V2.5 n=51) with hallucinations and omitted safety warnings.
links.quote: These discrepancies highlight a critical gap between knowledge possession and clinically reliable knowledge application, with direct implications for safe deployment.

links.outcome: Clinical knowledge errors, omissions, and missing safety warnings in guideline-based LBP responses
links.effect: Deepseek-V2.5 low-scoring responses: lack of safety warnings 16% (8/51), factual errors/hallucinations 12% (6/51); GPT-o3 harmful recommendations 7% (1/14).
links.quote: The most prominent causes of errors included: lack of safety warnings (Category 14: 16%, 8/51), factual errors/hallucinations (Category 1: 12%, 6/51), and incomplete or excessive content (Category 6: 10%, 5/51).

links.outcome: Reading difficulty and jargon in LLM outputs
links.effect: Excessive jargon was a near-universal error (e.g., GPT-5 23%, GPT-4o 20%); Deepseek-V2.5 highest reading difficulty score (16.871); outputs at secondary-school level.
links.quote: A near-universal pattern was the overuse of technical terminology, likely reflecting training biases toward guideline texts and specialist corpora during training.

links.outcome: Safety and completeness scores before vs after targeted safety prompt
links.effect: Deepseek-V2.5 safety improved 3.33 to 4.24 (B=0.91) and completeness 2.91 to 3.76 (B=0.86), p<0.001; GPT-4o safety gain non-significant (B=0.19, p=0.227).
links.quote: Linear mixed model estimates of marginal means ( Figure 5 and Table 4 ) showed that the corrected prompt significantly improved Deepseek-V2.5 across all five dimensions ( p < 0.001), with the largest gains in Safety ( B = 0.91, from 3.33 to 4.24) and Completeness ( B = 0.86, from 2.91 to 3.76).

links.outcome: Effect of prompt requiring accurate disclosure of uncertainty and safety precautions on response quality
links.effect: Prompt requiring safety verification, evidence-based statements and uncertainty disclosure significantly improved Deepseek-V2.5 on all five dimensions (p<0.001) and GPT-4o on four.
links.quote: Combined with moderate-to-large Hedges' g effect sizes, these findings provide preliminary evidence of the value of targeted prompt engineering, particularly for lower-performing models.

links.outcome: Comparative performance of five LLMs on LBP tasks
links.effect: Composite scores all >4.3; GPT-4o highest (4.593), Deepseek-V2.5 lowest (4.465); significant Deepseek deficits in accuracy, practicality, readability but not safety.
links.quote: As summarized in Table 2 , Deepseek-V2.5 scored the lowest on most dimensions.

unlisted_practices: Structured safety-oriented prompt engineering to reduce omissions and hallucinations in LLM clinical answers
Model selection by use-case risk (e.g., prioritizing more stable models for patient education or red-flag screening)

openai.sample_unit: questions (103 multiple-choice and 30 clinical scenario questions; 7 used in prompt intervention)

links.effect: All models exceeded 90% multiple-choice accuracy, yet clinical-scenario performance varied across guideline adherence, completeness, practicality, safety, and readability.
links.quote: Overall, although all models demonstrated strong foundational medical knowledge with overall multiple-choice question accuracy exceeding 90%, substantial variability emerged in guideline adherence, output completeness, practicality, safety, and readability when applied to realistic clinical scenarios.

links.effect: GPT-4o had lowest overall variance; Deepseek-V2.5 highest. Stability scores included GPT-4o accuracy 2.640* and safety 2.610*, Deepseek-V2.5 accuracy 3.330*.
links.quote: Deepseek-V2.5 exhibited the highest variance, reflecting the most unstable performance.

links.effect: Deepseek-V2.5 low-scoring responses: safety-warning omissions 16% (8/51), factual errors/hallucinations 12% (6/51), incomplete/excessive content 10% (5/51).
links.quote: The most prominent causes of errors included: lack of safety warnings (Category 14: 16%, 8/51), factual errors/hallucinations (Category 1: 12%, 6/51), and incomplete or excessive content (Category 6: 10%, 5/51).

links.effect: Deepseek-V2.5 highest reading difficulty score 16.871; Grok-4 15.827; recommended reading age highest for Grok-4 14.933, then Deepseek-V2.5 14.422.
links.quote: Deepseek-V2.5 received the highest reading difficulty score (16.871), indicating that its outputs require a higher level of text comprehension.

links.effect: Deepseek-V2.5 improved all five dimensions (p<0.001), largest in Safety B=0.91 (3.33 to 4.24) and Completeness B=0.86 (2.91 to 3.76).
links.quote: Linear mixed model estimates of marginal means ( Figure 5 and Table 4 ) showed that the corrected prompt significantly improved Deepseek-V2.5 across all five dimensions ( p < 0.001), with the largest gains in Safety ( B = 0.91, from 3.33 to 4.24) and Completeness ( B = 0.86, from 2.91 to 3.76).

links.outcome: gap between exam knowledge and clinical scenario guidance
links.effect: All 5 models scored >90% on licensing exam MCQs (90.29%-93.85%), but in clinical scenarios, lower-performing models produced safety-critical errors including factual hallucinations (12% of low scores) and omissions of safety warnings (16%).
links.quote: Overall, although all models demonstrated strong foundational medical knowledge with overall multiple-choice question accuracy exceeding 90%, substantial variability emerged in guideline adherence, output completeness, practicality, safety, and readability when applied to realistic clinical scenarios.

links.outcome: clinical response quality across five evaluation dimensions
links.effect: Targeted safety prompts significantly improved Deepseek-V2.5 across all 5 dimensions (p < 0.001; Safety B = 0.91, Completeness B = 0.86) and GPT-4o across 4 dimensions (Accuracy B = 0.76, Completeness B = 0.71, Practicality B = 0.48, Readability B = 0.38; Safety p = 0.227).
links.quote: Linear mixed model estimates of marginal means ( Figure 5 and Table 4 ) showed that the corrected prompt significantly improved Deepseek-V2.5 across all five dimensions ( p < 0.001), with the largest gains in Safety ( B = 0.91, from 3.33 to 4.24) and Completeness ( B = 0.86, from 2.91 to 3.76).
